title: Tree — Branch Initiation, Suppression, Plasticity, Pruning and Resource Cost
purpose: Deepen Tree beyond 'one becomes many' by incorporating regulated branching, environmental plasticity, resource allocation, pruning and branch death.
epistemic_rule: Plant branching biology is an empirical comparator. Project Tree remains symbolic/systemic; organizational or cultural branches are not literally botanical structures.
core_upgrade: Tree is regulated differentiation, not unlimited multiplication. Branches initiate under conditions, compete for resources, can remain dormant/suppressed, can be pruned, and may alter the whole architecture in response to environment.

branch_lifecycle.project_question: Where is latent branching capacity stored?
What signal/question/resource justifies a new branch?
What releases the branch from suppression/dormancy?
What resources and interfaces sustain growth?
What distinct function does the branch own?
When should duplication, dead ends or harmful growth be reduced?
How is provenance preserved after a branch closes?

regulation_rules: New branches are not automatically progress.
A branch should have a distinct function/owner rather than duplicate another branch.
Dormant branches can preserve option value without demanding public prominence.
Pruning can increase health when it removes duplication or dead weight, but destructive pruning can reduce resilience/diversity.
Architecture should respond to environmental/resource conditions without losing organism identity.
Root architecture and canopy architecture obey different constraints; do not use one generic branching metaphor for both.

project_applications.rooms: Create/split a Room only when a durable distinct ownership function emerges; otherwise keep a subtopic inside the parent.
project_applications.research: Open questions can remain dormant buds until evidence/resources justify activation.
project_applications.culture: Subcultures/roles branch from shared culture but can differentiate, merge, die or become parasitic/captured.
project_applications.works: Creative forms may branch without becoming knowledge owners.
project_applications.archive: Closed/superseded branches retain provenance even after public pruning.

findings: Root system architecture is highly plastic and adjusts branching in response to endogenous and environmental signals.
Root branching affects resource acquisition and anchorage, so branching has functional cost/benefit rather than being pure abundance.
Shoot branching is also regulated; classical apical-dominance models have been revised by broader hormonal and organ-level controls.

Modern shoot-branching models integrate sugar availability/signaling with auxin, cytokinin and strigolactone controls; branching is coordinated across organs rather than explained by a single top-down apical-dominance switch.
